skill.name: analytics-tracking
skill.description: Design, audit, and improve analytics tracking systems that produce reliable, decision-ready data. Use when the user wants to set up, fix, or evaluate analytics tracking (GA4, GTM, product analytics, events, conversions, UTMs). This skill focuses on measurement strategy, signal quality, and validation— not just firing events.
skill.summary: Design and audit analytics tracking systems for reliable, decision-ready data.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md context. Both flagged locations are benign markdown or analytics guidance, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 231 is a markdown code fence for an event naming pattern, followed by object_action[_context]. It does not execute shell commands or instruct the agent to run commands.
The phrase 'Avoid multiple containers' refers to Google Tag Manager container governance. It is not system reconnaissance and does not request host, network, or environment discovery.

content.value_statement: Teams often make decisions from analytics data that has not been validated. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design, audit, and improve tracking plans.
actual_capabilities: Scores measurement readiness with a 0 to 100 signal quality index.
Maps events and conversions to business decisions.
Designs event names, properties, triggers, and ownership notes.
Reviews GA4, GTM, UTM, and product analytics tracking plans.
Identifies duplicate firing, missing properties, PII risk, and inflated conversions.
Produces validation steps before analytics data is used for decisions.
limitations: It does not connect directly to GA4, GTM, or analytics platforms.
It cannot verify live event firing without logs, screenshots, or exported data.
It does not replace legal review for consent or privacy requirements.
It gives implementation guidance, but engineers must apply changes in the product.

use_cases.title: Repair Untrusted Marketing Data
use_cases.description: Audit campaign UTMs, conversions, and GA4 events before using reports for budget decisions.

use_cases.title: Design Product Event Taxonomy
use_cases.description: Create meaningful events and properties for activation, onboarding, and feature adoption analysis.

use_cases.title: Validate Analytics Implementation
use_cases.description: Review tracking requirements, GTM setup notes, and QA checks before a release.

prompt_templates.title: Score My Tracking Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit for an existing analytics setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my analytics setup and calculate the Measurement Readiness and Signal Quality Index. Ask for any missing context first.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Tracking Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Build an event plan for a product or website flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tracking plan for this user journey. Include events, properties, triggers, conversions, and the decision each signal supports.

prompt_templates.title: Find Conversion Tracking Risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a funnel before reporting or optimization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this conversion funnel for duplicate firing, weak conversion definitions, attribution gaps, PII risk, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Govern A Multi-Tool Analytics Stack
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across GA4, GTM, product analytics, and UTMs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this analytics stack across GA4, GTM, product analytics, and UTMs. Produce a prioritized remediation plan with owners and QA checks.

output_examples.input: We track page views, signup clicks, form starts, and completed signups, but the team does not trust GA4.
output_examples.output: A readiness score, key data quality risks, and a prioritized remediation order before optimization begins.

output_examples.input: We are launching onboarding and need events for activation analysis.
output_examples.output: A tracking plan with meaningful onboarding events, required properties, triggers, and supported product decisions.

output_examples.input: Our paid campaigns use mixed UTM names and conversions differ between tools.
output_examples.output: A UTM governance checklist, conversion definition review, and validation steps for consistent reporting.

best_practices: Start with the business decisions the data must support.
Validate event firing, properties, consent states, and duplicate behavior before reporting.
Document owners, naming rules, conversion definitions, and release checks.
anti_patterns: Tracking every click without a decision tied to the signal.
Treating GA4 or dashboard totals as true before validation.
Using free-text properties or PII in analytics events.

faq.question: Does this skill implement analytics code?
faq.answer: No. It creates strategy, audit findings, tracking plans, and validation steps for implementation.

faq.question: Can it work with GA4 and GTM?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GA4 and GTM guidance for events, conversions, containers, and validation.

faq.question: Does it support product analytics tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide event taxonomy and signal quality for tools such as Mixpanel and Amplitude.

faq.question: Can it check privacy compliance?
faq.answer: It can flag consent, PII, retention, and deletion considerations, but it is not legal advice.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide business goals, current events, conversions, tools, known data issues, and compliance constraints.

faq.question: What is the main output?
faq.answer: The main output is a readiness score, risk summary, tracking plan, conversion plan, and validation checklist.
